intent: I have old artificial turf at home, on HOA common land or on a business site in the Denver metro. Can I replace it after Colorado's 2026 rules, what does the new turf and base have to meet, does my city require worn turf to be replaced, and does a rebate or recycling route help?
distinctValue: The national replacement page is generic about approvals, base and disposal. This page covers what changes for a Denver-metro replacement. (1) Colorado's PFAS law (C.R.S. 25-15-605, SB24-081) bars anyone installing artificial turf with intentionally added PFAS on any property from 1 January 2026 while allowing pre-2026 turf to be maintained, so the replacement turf, home lots included, is what the rule reaches. (2) Three metro codes write replacement into upkeep: Northglenn 11-4-7(f)(6) and Thornton Water's 2026 rules (replace when maintenance or repair cannot simulate healthy living turf) and Brighton 8.04 (replace when it no longer simulates the infiltration of sod or native grasses), while Boulder's manual lets pre-7 March 2026 landscaping be maintained unless a project or site change requires compliance. (3) The base and slope standards a new install must meet in those cities (Northglenn road base, anchoring and six percent slope; Brighton 5 inches an hour percolation; Thornton three inches of compacted aggregate holding half an inch of rain). (4) Thornton's rebate eligibility is limited to turf replacing high-water lawn or bare new-construction ground, so swapping old artificial turf is not on its list. (5) For HOA and business land, the signed SB24-005 and HB25-1113 texts: the pre-2026 maintenance carve-out, the definition of maintain, the two-part redevelopment test, the open functional-turf list, the stricter-local-rule clause and the 2028 common-interest multifamily limb. The sports-field page covers the state rule for fields and the town pages each cover one city; none compares replacement triggers and new-install standards across metro cities or applies the PFAS installation rule to a replacement.

sources.label: Colorado General Assembly: SB24-081 signed act PDF (curl, pdftotext; 7 pages with signature and approval block)
supports: 25-15-605. Prohibition on the installation of artificial turf that contains intentionally added PFAS chemicals. (1) ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2026, A PERSON SHALL NOT INSTALL ARTIFICIAL TURF THAT CONTAINS INTENTIONALLY ADDED PFAS CHEMICALS ON ANY PORTION OF PROPERTY IN THE STATE.
(2) NOTHING IN THIS SECTION PROHIBITS A PERSON FROM MAINTAINING ARTIFICIAL TURF INSTALLED BEFORE JANUARY 1, 2026.

Section 3 adds definitions (1.5), (1.7), (2.5), (4)(c), (16.5), (16.7), (23.5) and (24.5) to 25-15-603; none shown defines artificial turf, so the page makes no claim about which parts of a turf system the rule reaches and only advises asking whether documentation covers backing and infill.

sources.label: Colorado General Assembly: SB24-005 signed act PDF (curl, pdftotext; 7 pages with signature and approval block)
supports: 37-99-102(1)(a) "APPLICABLE PROPERTY" MEANS: (I) COMMERCIAL, INSTITUTIONAL, OR INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY; (II) COMMON INTEREST COMMUNITY PROPERTY; OR (III) A STREET RIGHT-OF-WAY, PARKING LOT, MEDIAN, OR TRANSPORTATION CORRIDOR.

37-99-102(5) "COMMON INTEREST COMMUNITY PROPERTY" MEANS PROPERTY WITHIN A COMMON INTEREST COMMUNITY THAT IS OWNED AND MAINTAINED BY A UNIT OWNERS' ASSOCIATION, SUCH AS ENTRYWAYS, PARKS, AND OTHER COMMON ELEMENTS AS DEFINED IN SECTION 38-33.3-103 (5).
37-99-102(9) "LOCAL ENTITY" MEANS A: (a) HOME RULE OR STATUTORY CITY, COUNTY, CITY AND COUNTY, TERRITORIAL CHARTER CITY, OR TOWN; (b) SPECIAL DISTRICT; AND (c) METROPOLITAN DISTRICT.

37-99-102(10) "MAINTAIN" OR "MAINTAINING" MEANS AN ACTION TO PRESERVE THE EXISTING STATE OF NONFUNCTIONAL TURF, ARTIFICIAL TURF, OR AN INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES THAT HAS ALREADY BEEN INSTALLED, PLANTED, OR PLACED.

37-99-102(14) "REDEVELOPMENT PROJECT" MEANS A CONSTRUCTION PROJECT THAT: (a) REQUIRES A BUILDING OR LANDSCAPING PERMIT, PLAN CHECK, OR DESIGN REVIEW; AND (b) RESULTS IN A DISTURBANCE OF MORE THAN FIFTY PERCENT OF THE AGGREGATE LANDSCAPE AREA.

37-99-103(1) ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2026, A LOCAL ENTITY SHALL NOT INSTALL, PLANT, OR PLACE, OR ALLOW ANY PERSON TO INSTALL, PLANT, OR PLACE, ANY NONFUNCTIONAL TURF, ARTIFICIAL TURF, OR INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES, AS PART OF A NEW DEVELOPMENT PROJECT OR REDEVELOPMENT PROJECT, ON ANY PORTION OF APPLICABLE PROPERTY WITHIN THE LOCAL ENTITY'S JURISDICTION.

37-99-103(4) NOTHING IN THIS SECTION PROHIBITS: (a) A LOCAL ENTITY FROM MAINTAINING, OR ALLOWING ANY PERSON TO MAINTAIN, ANY NONFUNCTIONAL TURF, ARTIFICIAL TURF, OR INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES INSTALLED, PLANTED, OR PLACED BEFORE JANUARY 1, 2026; ... (d) A LOCAL ENTITY OR THE DEPARTMENT FROM ESTABLISHING PROHIBITIONS ON, OR REQUIREMENTS FOR, NONFUNCTIONAL TURF, ARTIFICIAL TURF, OR INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES THAT ARE MORE STRINGENT THAN THE REQUIREMENTS OF THIS SECTION; OR (e) A LOCAL ENTITY OR THE DEPARTMENT FROM INSTALLING, OR ALLOWING ANY PERSON TO INSTALL, ARTIFICIAL TURF ON ATHLETIC FIELDS OF PLAY.

sources.label: Colorado General Assembly: HB25-1113 act as passed PDF (curl, pdftotext; 8 pages, enrolled text prepared for signature; enactment confirmed on the bill page)
supports: SECTION 2. In Colorado Revised Statutes, 37-99-102, amend (1)(a)(II), (1)(a)(III), (7), and (17); repeal (1)(b); and add (1)(a)(IV), (1.5), (6.5), (10.5), (12.5), (14.5), and (18.5)
(1.5) "APPLICABLE RESIDENTIAL REAL PROPERTY" MEANS A MULTIFAMILY RESIDENTIAL HOUSING PREMISES PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES MORE THAN TWELVE DWELLING UNITS.

(6.5) "FUNCTIONAL ARTIFICIAL TURF" MEANS ARTIFICIAL TURF THAT IS: (a) LOCATED IN A RECREATIONAL USE AREA OR OTHER SPACE THAT IS REGULARLY USED FOR CIVIC, COMMUNITY, OR RECREATIONAL PURPOSES, WHICH MAY INCLUDE A PLAYGROUND, A SPORTS FIELD, A PICNIC GROUND, AN AMPHITHEATER, A PORTION OF A PARK, AND THE PLAYING AREA OF A GOLF COURSE, SUCH AS A DRIVING RANGE, CHIPPING AND PUTTING GREEN, TEE BOX, GREEN, FAIRWAY, AND ROUGH; OR (b) A COMPONENT OF A PRODUCT DESIGNED AND APPROVED BY A PROFESSIONAL ENGINEER FOR CIVIL INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
(10.5) "MULTIFAMILY RESIDENTIAL HOUSING PREMISES PROPERTY" MEANS COMMON INTEREST PROPERTY SUCH AS ENTRYWAYS, PARKS, AND OTHER COMMON ELEMENTS AS DEFINED IN SECTION 38-33.3-103 (5).

37-99-103(1) as amended: On and after January 1, 2026, a local entity shall not install, plant, or place, or allow any person to install, plant, or place, any nonfunctional turf, NONFUNCTIONAL artificial turf, or invasive plant species, as part of a new development project or redevelopment project, on any portion of applicable property within the local entity's jurisdiction.

37-99-103(4)(a) as amended: A local entity from maintaining, or allowing any person to maintain, any nonfunctional turf, NONFUNCTIONAL ARTIFICIAL TURF, artificial turf, or invasive plant species installed, planted, or placed before January 1, 2026; (4)(d) kept: more stringent local prohibitions or requirements; (4)(e): artificial turf on athletic fields of play.

37-99-103(5)(a) ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2028, A LOCAL ENTITY SHALL NOT INSTALL, PLANT, OR PLACE, OR ALLOW A PERSON TO INSTALL, PLANT, OR PLACE, ANY NONFUNCTIONAL TURF, NONFUNCTIONAL ARTIFICIAL TURF, OR INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES, AS PART OF A NEW DEVELOPMENT PROJECT OR REDEVELOPMENT PROJECT, ON ANY PORTION OF APPLICABLE PROPERTIES THAT INCLUDE MULTIFAMILY RESIDENTIAL HOUSING PREMISES PROPERTY.

sources.label: Colorado General Assembly: HB25-1113 bill page (headless Chromium)
supports: The act expands the definition of "applicable property" to include a multifamily residential housing premises property that includes more than 12 dwelling units (applicable residential real property).

The act prohibits a local entity, on and after January 1, 2028, from installing, planting, or placing, or allowing a person to install, plant, or place, any nonfunctional turf, nonfunctional artificial turf, or invasive plant species, as part of a new development project or redevelopment project, on applicable properties that include multifamily residential housing premises property.
(Note: This summary applies to this bill as enacted.) Status: Became Law

sources.label: Northglenn Municipal Code, Article 11-4 Development Standards, section 11-4-7 (headless Chromium; section source note Ord. 1766, 2019; 1782, 2019; 1848, 2023; 1870, 2025)
supports: 11-4-7(b)(1) New Development. Unless otherwise exempted in Subsection 11-4-7(b)(3) below, or elsewhere in this UDO, the standards in Section 11-4-7 shall apply to all new development and land uses. (2) Expansions and Enlargements. ... the standards in Section 11-4-7 shall apply to the following expansions and enlargements: (A) Any site improvements requiring full compliance pursuant to 11-1-5(f)(3) ... (B) The expansion or enlargement of a use or structure that requires a special use permit; or (C) Major parking area improvements

(f) Artificial Turf Regulations. (3) Installation: Artificial turf shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications and maintained in a manner to mimic healthy living turf, including the following: (A) Sod or existing groundcover shall be removed prior to installation of any artificial turf. (B) Artificial turf shall be installed over a compacted and porous road base material. (C) Artificial turf shall be anchored at all edges and seams.
(4) Slope restrictions: Artificial turf shall not be installed on slopes greater than six percent.

(6) Maintenance: The following maintenance activities are required for artificial turf; cleaning, sanitizing, brushing and removal of debris, cleaning shall be done with biodegradable products, repairing of depressions to maintain an even visual surface, regular maintenance to eliminate any orders, flat or matted areas, weeds, looseness at edges, seams or elsewhere, replacement of the artificial turf when maintenance or repair is unable to simulate a healthy living turf.

sources.label: City of Brighton Land Use code, Article 8, 8.04 Plant Specifications (Municode, headless Chromium; section history Ord. No. 2438, 1-2-2024)
supports: Artificial Turf: The chosen material and any underlayment installed below the turf shall have a minimum percolation rate of 5 inches per hour. The liner material and all bedding shall be permeable to allow for infiltration of water into the soil below to mimic conditions of sod and natural grasses.
Artificial turf shall be cleaned and debris removed on a regular basis. Artificial turf shall be replaced when it is no longer simulating the infiltration properties of sod or native grasses.

sources.label: Thornton Water: 2026 Artificial Turf Rules for Water-Wise Landscape Rebate, Information and Requirements (PDF, curl and pdftotext; every page footed 1/1/2026)
supports: PFAS-free Requirements: All artificial turf, infill, and other manufactured products used to install artificial turf shall be free of per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).
"PFC-free" shall not be sufficient to satisfy this requirement.

Documentation showing that the proposed product is PFAS-free shall be submitted at the time of permit application, and approval of such documentation will be at the sole discretion of the director or designee.

Installation: 3. Sub-base must be a minimum of three inches deep of compacted aggregate material, which may be a combination of course and fine material layers separated by a geotextile per the manufacturer's specifications. The specified base material(s) system must contain a minimum of one-half inch of precipitation before generating sheet flow runoff.
General Maintenance: 6. Replacement of the artificial turf when maintenance or repair cannot simulate a healthy living turf.

Rebate Requirements: 1. ... To be eligible for the rebate, artificial turf must replace an area of high-water demand lawn, such as Kentucky Bluegrass, on existing residential lots or areas of no landscaping on new construction residential lots.
A Minor Development Permit is required before the installation of artificial turf as landscaping.

supports: Artificial turf is prohibited in all new development, unless it is functional artificial turf.

A case-insensitive search of the page text for turf, carpet and rug returned no match. The page says only that the list had no turf or carpet category when checked, not that turf cannot be recycled anywhere.

notUsed: City of Westminster Landscape Regulations PDF (DocumentCenter/View/1138): opened 12 September 2026 (curl, pdftotext, pdfinfo), the document is headed LANDSCAPE REGULATIONS 2004, 'Effective Date September 1, 2004', '2004 Edition', PDF created 24 April 2017; DocumentCenter/View/1398, which the city's site search lists as 'Landscape Regulations (PDF) Nov 14, 2024', is a byte-identical copy. It predates the SB24-005 and HB25-1113 local adoption deadlines. Westminster posted a May 2026 Public Review Draft Unified Development Code (DocumentCenter/View/6951, June 23, 2026 Planning Commission packet) whose 11-7-1(D)(3)(k) rewrites the artificial turf rules and says only that turf 'shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications and maintained to mimic healthy living turf'; its effective date is blank, so it is a draft. Neither is presented as Westminster's current replacement rule.

Western Resource Advocates 'Senate Bill 24-005 Made Simple' guide and the WRA 'Local Compliance with Colorado Senate Bill 24-005' handout posted in a Town of Fraser agenda packet: secondary summaries. Their statement that only the disturbed portion of a redeveloped parcel must conform is WRA's reading, not statutory text, so it is not used. The statutory definitions are taken from the signed SB24-005 act and the HB25-1113 act text, both of which download from leg.colorado.gov/bill_files (45372 and 82792).

Colorado Geological Survey expansive soil page: its clay and landscaping findings already appear on the pet-turf page, several town pages and two articles, so the base block is written from the metro code standards instead.
Colorado Division of Real Estate HB25-1113 material: the multifamily date conflict it creates is reported on the colorado-hoa-turf-rules guide, which the FAQ links to rather than restating.

Denver Solid Waste Management large item pickup and Denver Arapahoe Disposal Site pages on denvergov.org: navigation timed out in headless Chromium and curl could not connect on 12 September 2026. No Denver-metro landfill or drop-off rule for artificial turf could be confirmed, so the page names none.

Aurora UDO 146-4.7.3.B.11 artificial turf standards: only archived 2022-2023 text is on file (aurora-co evidence); the live code was not opened, so Aurora's maintenance wording is not presented as current.
unresolved: Whether a full strip-and-relay of pre-2026 nonfunctional artificial turf on applicable property is maintenance (defined as preserving the existing state of turf already installed) or a new installation is not answered by SB24-005 or HB25-1113; the page says so and tells the reader to ask the planning office and any reviewing district.

Whether Northglenn 11-4-7 and Brighton 8.04 apply to replacing turf on an existing lot outside a new development, expansion or approved plan is not settled by the text opened; the page qualifies both with 'where those standards apply' and tells the reader to ask the planning office.

Thornton's document is framed as rules for the water-wise landscape rebate, though it cites the Thornton City Code and says a Minor Development Permit is required before installing artificial turf as landscaping; the page attributes each point to Thornton Water's 2026 rules and does not claim the city code itself was opened.

The multifamily compliance date is disputed in published guidance (see the colorado-hoa-turf-rules guide). The HB25-1113 act text sets 1 January 2028 at 37-99-103(5)(a) for common interest property in multifamily housing of more than twelve units; whether a single-owner rental complex has such property is not settled, and the FAQ tells the reader to ask.
